title: Coleman Hawkins's lateness and Henderson's threats to fire him
summary: Henderson threatens to fire Hawkins for arriving late, but the band pleads for him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Well, Fletcher was a very -- he was a fellow that -- he was strict and nice and exact in everything he did. But he wasn't satisfied with his band. And he threatened to fire Coleman Hawkins more than once, because Coleman used to come in late. Sometimes we'd open up and start playing, and here comes Coleman. But when he'd get up there and pick that horn up, everybody was satisfied.
But Fletcher didn't like it. But the band predomi-
nated and pleaded, please don't do it. Where are you going to get another saxophone player like him? You couldn't get another tenor in New York like Coleman. Coleman was great.
